shared_elements: T-shaped monolithic stone pillar with broad head and narrower shaft
low-relief carving on the flat face
elongated serpentine/limb-like relief running down the shaft
horizontal division of the carved surface into upper and lower fields
weathered pale limestone surface set in an excavated stone-walled trench
justification: Both are T-shaped pillars of the same pale stone bearing shallow, flat-relief animals in strict profile, with a quadruped occupying the upper field and long sinuous forms trailing down the shaft below a horizontal division. The clearest difference is density and legibility: B carries a crowded multi-register programme (row of creatures across the head, a zigzag/net band, birds and a large bird below) while A shows only one badly eroded animal and a few faint linear motifs on an otherwise blank shaft.
